reserved.for: Task 6: the recreated study corner (EIN-M-0013, EIN-M-0014)

narration.text: Albert Einstein had a home study at 112 Mercer Street, Princeton, New Jersey.
Albert Einstein was working as a consultant to the United States Government during World War II.
Albert Einstein was doing research for the Bureau of Ordnance, in his study at Princeton, N.J.
Nine letters were written by Albert Einstein to Lieutenant Stephen Brunauer of the Research and Development Division.
The letters relate to Albert Einstein's research with the Research and Development Division of the Navy, specifically underwater explosions and a proposed electromagnetic torpedo detonator.

Albert Einstein's letter of June 18, 1943 to Lieutenant Stephen Brunauer discusses Albert Einstein's idea of an electro-magnetic device that will automatically explode a torpedo as it passes underneath a ship.
In a letter of July 30, 1943, Albert Einstein reveals that he has come up with a mathematical simplification to analyze the impact an underwater explosion would have on the hull of an armored ship.
Signed copies of a contract and naturalization papers were enclosed with Albert Einstein's letter of August 13, 1943 to Lieutenant Stephen Brunauer.
112 Mercer Street remained Albert Einstein's home until his death in 1955.
In this room, a corner recreates Einstein's study at Princeton, N.J., as two 1943 National Archives photographs show it.
